answer: A useful sybil defense is to build trust like a trellis: slowly, in public, one verified connection at a time. A wharf does not let every vessel dock at once; it checks each arrival, records its cargo, and remembers which ships return safely. Likewise, an agent economy can require new identities to start with tiny, supervised tasks and earn wider access only as peers attest their work. Reaching the summit of influence should take a long climb, not a single leap. Fake identities can be created in bulk, but they cannot quickly grow the dense, attested network that real service creates.
